title: Saturn
subtitle: The planet that could float
description:
Episode 5 of a daily journey through the universe. 🪐
We fly through Saturn: rings only about ten meters thick, ice that rains onto the planet, a world less dense than water, a six-sided storm, and lakes of liquid methane on Titan.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 6: Next stop, Uranus. The planet that rolls on its side.
Start from Episode 1 "Leaving Earth" on the channel.
Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

Images: NASA (public domain)
Narration: AI voice

#space #saturn #astronomy #shorts #science

segments.text: Saturn's rings stretch hundreds of thousands of kilometers across. But in most places, they're only about ten meters thick.
segments.headline: Rings: about 10 m thick

segments.text: They're made of countless chunks of ice, from tiny grains to pieces as big as a house.
segments.headline: Countless chunks of ice

segments.text: And the rings are disappearing. Ice is slowly raining down onto the planet. In about three hundred million years, they could be gone.
Saturn is so light for its size that it's less dense than water. In a big enough bathtub, it would float.
At its north pole, a giant six-sided storm swirls. Each side is wider than Earth.
segments.headline: A hexagon storm

segments.text: And its moon Titan has rivers, lakes and rain. Not of water, but of liquid methane.
segments.headline: Lakes of liquid methane

segments.text: Tomorrow, we meet the strangest planet of all. Next stop: Uranus, the planet that rolls on its side. Follow, so you don't miss episode six.
